audit.why: The prose addresses the owner in second person, so third-person pronouns refer to the enemy. These templates were authored for a male enemy and only the champion name was substituted, leaving the pronouns wrong. champ-data/champ-gender.js is the authority.

edits.before: At level 1 Galio has the edge: his Q double-wind and empowered auto out-range Rell, who is melee and weakest before her W dismount tools come online. Poke her down while she can only walk at you. Once she gets W she gains a real engage, so bank your early advantage before that.
edits.after: At level 1 Galio has the edge: her Q double-wind and empowered auto out-range Rell, who is melee and weakest before her W dismount tools come online. Poke her down while she can only walk at you. Once she gets W she gains a real engage, so bank your early advantage before that.

edits.before: Through the mid levels Rell takes over: her mounted W crash and E stun give her a hard, reliable engage that out-trades Galio's slower walk-up, and she can lock him or his ADC down. Galio must hold E-flash and taunt for the moment she commits rather than trading blows. Her armor/MR shred also makes her all-ins hurt more than his.

edits.before: In late teamfights the two tanks trade blows but Galio's global Hero's Entrance is the tiebreaker: he can flip a fight from off-screen or peel his carry out of Rell's dive, while Rell's Magnet Storm needs her in the middle of the enemy. Galio's W also blunts magic damage around Rell's pull. Well-timed R plus taunt lets Galio out-impact her engage in the final fights.
